Aerobic fitness has been found to have a positive relationship with microvascular function in healthy adults at risk of developing Type 2 diabetes. Specifically, individuals with higher levels of aerobic fitness also tend to have better microvascular and endothelial responsiveness.

In more detail, this is reflected in studies that suggest that maximal oxygen uptake (VO2 max) was not reduced in people who were at risk of developing Type 2 diabetes compared to healthy controls. However, even among those at risk, individuals with higher levels of aerobic fitness also had improved microvascular and endothelial function.

This suggests that regular aerobic exercise may be beneficial for improving cardiovascular health in people at risk of developing Type 2 diabetes, and may help to reduce the risk of complications associated with the condition.
